name: Glenn T. Seaborg
summary: American chemist who led the Berkeley group discovering plutonium and other transuranium elements.

name: Arthur C. Wahl
summary: Graduate student and key collaborator of Seaborg who performed critical chemical separations.

name: Joseph W. Kennedy
summary: Instructor and collaborator of Seaborg who developed radiation detection instrumentation.

name: John W. Gofman
summary: Graduate student of Seaborg who worked on protoactinium and uranium-233.

name: Emilio Segrè
summary: Physicist and collaborator of Seaborg on plutonium fissionability experiments.

name: Edwin M. McMillan
summary: Physicist who co-discovered neptunium and collaborated with Seaborg on element 94.

name: Enrico Fermi
summary: Physicist who advised Seaborg on plutonium production and fissionability tests.

name: Ernest Lawrence
summary: Physicist and director of the Berkeley Radiation Laboratory who supported Seaborg's work.

name: Lyman J. Briggs
summary: Chairman of the Uranium Committee who received Seaborg's reports.

name: Vannevar Bush
summary: Director of the Office of Scientific Research and Development.

name: Gilbert N. Lewis
summary: Chemist and Dean of the College of Chemistry at Berkeley who supported Seaborg.

aliases: The Regents of the University of California
name: University of California, Berkeley
summary: University where Seaborg conducted the early heavy isotope research.

name: Department of Chemistry, Berkeley
summary: Academic department employing Seaborg and his group.

name: University of Chicago
summary: University where the Metallurgical Laboratory was located.

name: Metallurgical Laboratory
summary: Laboratory at Chicago where Seaborg moved in 1942.

name: Uranium Committee
summary: Government committee overseeing uranium research.

name: National Defense Research Committee
summary: Committee that funded Seaborg's research contracts.

aliases: Office for Emergency Management, Office of Scientific Research and Development
name: Office of Scientific Research and Development
summary: Agency that succeeded the NDRC.

name: Gilman Hall
summary: Chemistry building at Berkeley where Seaborg's lab was located.

name: Crocker Laboratory
summary: Laboratory at Berkeley housing the cyclotrons.

name: Plutonium
summary: Transuranium element discovered by Seaborg's group.

name: Neptunium
summary: Transuranium element studied by Seaborg's group.

name: Sample A
summary: Large sample of plutonium-239 produced in March 1941.

name: Sample F
summary: Larger sample of plutonium-239 produced in July 1941.

name: 60-inch cyclotron
summary: Particle accelerator at Berkeley used for bombardments.

name: 37-inch cyclotron
summary: Smaller particle accelerator at Berkeley used for fission tests.
